About me

Calm, method and a bag you can actually carry.

I belong to the generation that learned to sort things out without a mobile phone. After a blackout caught me holding a torch with dead batteries, I set out to learn how to really prepare. Today I help families and teams in several countries build bags that are light, useful and checked. I don't sell fear: I teach you to decide what to take and keep it within reach.

Your first 72 hours

The basics to get through three days while help arrives or normal life returns.

  • WaterAbout 3 litres per person per day across your bag, stored supply and a filter.
  • FoodNo cooking, easy to open and already to your taste.
  • First aidBasic dressings and your medication with written instructions.
  • Light and powerHeadlamp, batteries and a charged power bank.
  • DocumentsCopies in a waterproof pouch and some cash.
  • WarmthLayers, rain cover and a thermal blanket.
  • CommunicationRadio, whistle and phone numbers on paper.

Frequently asked questions

How heavy should the bag be?

As a guide, 10 to 15% of your body weight. What matters is that you can walk with it.

How much does preparing cost?

Start with things you already own and build up gradually. You get the price of each service before we begin.

Do you ship bags?

I prepare a list with shops in your country. For assembled bags, ask me about availability and shipping.

What about medication?

Ask your doctor or pharmacist how much to keep and how to store it, and rotate it before it expires.

Which documents should I pack?

Copies of ID, insurance, prescriptions and contacts, protected from water.

How often should I check it?

Twice a year, for instance when the clocks change, and always after using it.
